Eat Like an Athlete, Not Like a Dieter

Dieters ask what they can cut. Athletes ask what they need. That one question changes everything on your plate.

The dieter's mindset is built on restriction: less, smaller, skip it. The athlete's mindset is built on performance: what will make me stronger tomorrow?

Same food. Completely different relationship with it.

Food is fuel, not the enemy

When you train hard, under-eating doesn't make you disciplined — it makes you slower, weaker and hungrier. Energy is what lets you show up, push the last set and recover for the next one.

Protein first

Protein is the raw material for repairing and building muscle. Many sports nutrition guidelines land somewhere around 1.6 grams per kilogram of bodyweight per day for people lifting seriously. You don't need to be exact — just build every meal around a solid protein source.

Build the plate around what builds you.

The athlete's plate

  • A palm or two of protein — eggs, chicken, fish, beans, yoghurt, tofu.
  • A fist of carbs — rice, oats, potatoes, fruit. More on heavy training days.
  • Two fists of vegetables — colour isn't our brand, but it should be on your plate.
  • A thumb of fats — olive oil, nuts, avocado.

Consistency beats perfection

You don't need a perfect diet. You need a good one you can repeat. Eighty percent solid choices, every week, will beat a flawless plan you abandon by Thursday.

Everyone's needs are different — if you have a medical condition or specific goals, a registered dietitian is worth every penny.
